result_text:
Promotions now carry an optional description, and it comes back from all six listing and lookup paths. The promotion-related test classes pass (`PromotionTest`, `PromotionUsageTest`, `PromotionsPerRegionTest`, `PromotionsPerCustomerTest`, `PriceListTest`, `OrderPromotionTest`), and nothing is committed.

What changed:
- **`schema.sql`**: new nullable `description VARCHAR(200)` column on `promotion`.
- **`model/Promotion.java`**: `description` is the last record component. Null means no description.
- **`service/PromotionService.java`**: new six-argument `createPromotion(..., category, description)`. A blank description is stored as null. The existing five-argument method delegates with null, so current callers are unchanged.
- **`DataStorePart09.java`**: the insert writes the description. The promotion lookup by code, active-on-date, active-in-region, by-category and best-promotion queries select it and map it.
- **`DataStorePart10.java`**: the unused-promotions query selects and maps it too.
- **`PromotionTest.java`**: new `keepsDescriptionOfPromotion` test. It checks a promotion created with "Summer sale on all hardware" keeps the text in the active, category and region listings, and that a blank one reads back as null.

Two things to be aware of:
- The 200-character limit is not checked in Java, so a longer description would fail at insert with an `IllegalStateException`.
- I did not add a description to the demo data (e.g. `SUMMER10` in `DemoScenario`), so demo promotions show none.
